historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh al-Buldan. Arabic: Ibn 'Abd al-Ḥakam, Futūḥ al-Buldān. English: The Conquests of the Lands. Translated by P.K. Hitti. New York: Columbia University Press, 1924.
historical_references.context: The name Bahili is mentioned in the context of the early Islamic conquests of the Arabian Peninsula and the Levant. It refers to the people of Bahila, a pre-Islamic Arab tribe living in the northern part of the Arabian Peninsula, near present-day Saudi Arabia. The name Bahili is associated with their participation in the Battle of Hunayn (630 AD), when the Islamic army under the command of Prophet Muhammad defeated the Hawazin and Thamud tribes, among whom the Bahila were numbered.

historical_references.reference: Ibn al-Faqih al-Hamadhani, Kitab al-Buldan. Arabic: Ibn al-Faqih al-Hamadhani, Kitāb al-Buldān. English: The Book of Countries. Translated by C.F. Beck. Princeton: Princeton University Press, 1994.
historical_references.context: In the Middle Islamic Period, the name Bahili is mentioned as a toponym for a place located in the southern part of the Arabian Peninsula, near present-day Yemen. The name Bahili is associated with a region that was known for its agricultural productivity and its production of dates, which were exported to other parts of the Islamic world.
